# Nyra

> Nyra is a small, strictly typed programming language for code that AI agents write and then run unsupervised: nearly as cheap to write as Python, native-fast, and (from v0.6) unable to touch anything it did not declare. One `.nyra` file compiles to a native executable (through C), or to C, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust or Go source, with the `nyra` command line tool. It has no semicolons, no implicit conversions, no shadowing and no null, values are copied instead of shared, and its compiler reports every error as a stable code with an exact position and a fix hint (`nyra check file.nyra --json`). Capabilities (`--allow fs`, deny by default) are coming in v0.6; today a program has the rights of its process, so run code you do not trust in a container or VM. Measured on 83 tasks: first-try pass Opus 98%, Sonnet 96%, Haiku 4.5 66% (Python 78%); about 1.2-1.3x Python's code tokens and fewer than Rust's; about 5-6 ms against about 300 ms for Python on the speed tasks (`bench/published/`).

Nyra is new and is not in your training data. It looks a little like Rust, Go and TypeScript but it is none of them: do not guess syntax, and do not use anything the docs below do not describe (there are no tuples and no modules of your own yet; maps are `[str: int]`, `["a": 1]`, `m[k]`, `m.get(k, 0)`; the standard library is imported with `use input`, `use os`, `use fs`, `use json`, `use time`, `use random`, `use math` and `use text`, and called as `math.sqrt(x)`). Read the AI guide before you write code.

This file describes Nyra v0.5. Check the version you have with `nyra --version`: an older compiler lacks some of what is described here, and Nyra is pre-1.0, so the syntax may still change.

The ten most important rules for writing correct Nyra (v0.5):

1. A program is a script: its statements stand at the top level and run in order, so do not write `fn main()` (it is allowed, but costs tokens). `fn` and `struct` definitions may appear anywhere. The script's top-level `let`/`var` variables are visible in every function, which may change the `var`s (`var pos = 0` then `fn advance() { pos += 1 }`): no need to pass them as parameters. Declare them before the first call that uses them.
2. No semicolons. One statement per line. Braces are required and `{` stays on the same line as `fn`, `if`, `else`, `while` and `for`. Comments are `// ...`.
3. Types are `int` (64-bit), `float`, `bool`, `str`, `char` (`'a'`), arrays `[T]` (`[1, 2, 3]`) and structs. Parameters and return types are always written (`fn add(a: int, b: int) -> int`); local types are inferred, but an empty array needs one: `var xs: [int] = []`.
4. Types never convert implicitly: `1 + 2.0` and `"n=" + 5` are errors. Write `float(x)`, `int(x)` or `str(x)`, and write float literals with a dot (`2.0`, never `2`).
5. `let` is immutable and `var` is mutable: only a `var` can be reassigned or changed (`n += 1`, `xs.push(4)`, `p.x = 3`). A name can be declared only once while it is visible (no shadowing). Parameters are immutable unless declared `inout`, and then the call says `inout` too: `swap(inout a, inout b)`.
6. Conditions must be `bool`: `if n != 0 { }`, never `if n { }`. The boolean operators are `&&`, `||` and `!`.
7. Return with `ret`, not `return`. A function with `-> T` must end every path with `ret`. One-line form: `fn square(x: int) -> int = x * x`.
8. `for i in 0..10 { }` counts 0 to 9 (the end is exclusive, there is no `..=`), `for x in xs { }` visits each element and `for c in s { }` each char; `while cond { }` also exists. `break` and `continue` act on the innermost loop.
9. Text: `+` joins two strings and `"sum: {a + b}"` inserts any value (a `{` or `}` that starts no value is plain text). `s.len()` counts characters and `s[i]` is a `char`, compared with single quotes: `s[0] == 'a'`. Chars convert explicitly: `str(c)`, `c.code()`, `char(65)`. Strings and arrays have methods (`split`, `replace`, `trim`, `upper`, `index_of`, `push`, `pop`, `sort`, `join`, `slice`, ...); there is no `len(x)`. `xs.map(x => x * 2)`, `xs.filter(x => x > 0)`, `xs.sum()` and `[x * x for x in xs if x > 0]` build values.
10. A struct is declared `struct Point { x: int, y: int }`, built with every field named in order, `Point(x: 1, y: 2)`, and has no methods: write `fn area(p: Point) -> int`. Assigning or passing an array or a struct copies it. `print(a, b)` prints values of any type, separated by spaces, and arrays and structs as Nyra code; a last `end: ""` replaces the newline: `print(x, end: " ")`. A failing operation (index out of bounds, integer division by zero, `int("12x")`) stops the program with a runtime error and exit code 101. An int overflow stops the program (E0255; ints never wrap), and with `--js` an int beyond 2^53 - 1 does too (E0256): for a hash, keep it small with `%` at every step.

Catch logic mistakes before running: after each non-trivial function write 1-2 examples with values worked out by hand, `fn sq(x: int) -> int = x * x   ex sq(3) == 9, sq(-2) == 4` (or `ex ...` on the line after a function's closing `}`). The compiler evaluates them while it compiles (they are never part of the program) and reports a false one as E0250 with the actual and expected value; `nyra test prog.nyra --json` lists them all.

How to check your work: `nyra check prog.nyra --json` prints `{"ok":true,"errors":[]}` or a list of errors, each with `code`, `line`, `col`, `message` and `hint`. Fix them all and check again, then `nyra run prog.nyra` (add `--js` to use Node.js instead of a C compiler).

Let the compiler repair simple mistakes first: `nyra check prog.nyra --json --fix` applies every error that has exactly one possible repair (`return` -> `ret`, a `;`, `elif`, `and`, `True`, `'text'`, `xs.length()`, `string`, `Point { x: 1 }`, `5.`), checks again, and writes the file back if it then compiles (`run --fix` then runs it). Such errors also carry the repair as `"fix":[{"line":..,"col":..,"end_line":..,"end_col":..,"text":".."}]` (replace from `line`:`col` up to, not including, `end_line`:`end_col`; columns count characters). Use `--fix` or apply the `fix` edits before asking a model to repair the program: it costs no model call. If you cannot run commands, state the output the program should print and tell the user to run `nyra run prog.nyra`.

MCP: `nyra mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server (stdio) built into the compiler; add it with `claude mcp add nyra -- nyra mcp` or `{"command":"nyra","args":["mcp"]}`. Its tools are `nyra_spec` (this language's spec), `nyra_check`, `nyra_test`, `nyra_run` (native or JS), `nyra_explain` and `nyra_build`, so an agent needs no files or shell.

Editing: to change a program that exists, do not resend it. `nyra outline prog.nyra` lists its functions and structs with line ranges, `nyra show prog.nyra name` prints one, and `nyra edit prog.nyra` takes new definitions on stdin (each replaces the symbol of its name) or commands (`@replace NAME`, `@add after NAME`, `@delete NAME`, `@rename NAME NEW`, `@add-field Struct name: type`). The rest of the file stays byte-identical, and an edit that adds errors is refused. The MCP tools `nyra_outline`, `nyra_show` and `nyra_edit` do the same.

## Docs

- [AI guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/docs/AI_GUIDE.md): read this first. The workflow, every rule as do and don't, what does not exist yet, all error codes with fixes, recipes and complete programs.
- [Language spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/docs/SPEC.md): the complete language: types, operators, builtins, every method of strings, chars and arrays, structs, `inout`, memory control, printing, runtime errors and known backend differences.
- [Error database](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/docs/ERRORS.md): every error code with what it means, the usual causes, and a wrong and a fixed program; `nyra explain E0201 --json` prints an entry.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/README.md): overview, install, CLI options and roadmap.

## Examples

Every example has a matching `.out` file with the exact expected output, and runs on both backends.

- [hello.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/hello.nyra): the smallest program
- [fizzbuzz.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/fizzbuzz.nyra): `for`, `else if`, `%`
- [strings.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/strings.nyra): joining, comparing, searching, slicing and converting strings
- [chars.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/chars.nyra): `char` values, codes and character tests
- [arrays.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/arrays.nyra): every array method, nested arrays, printing
- [structs.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/structs.nyra): declaring, building, changing and comparing structs
- [inout.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/inout.nyra): functions that change the caller's variables
- [globals.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/globals.nyra): script variables used and changed by functions (a small parser)
- [loops.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/loops.nyra): `break` and `continue`
- [memory.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/memory.nyra): `free`, `arena` and `keep`
- [fib.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/fib.nyra): recursion
- [primes.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/primes.nyra): `while`, early `ret`, string comparison
- [math.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/math.nyra): floats, explicit conversions, Newton's method
- [gcd.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/gcd.nyra): Euclid's algorithm, `lcm`
- [interpolation.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/interpolation.nyra): `"{expr}"` strings
- [if_value.nyra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/examples/if_value.nyra): `if` as a value

## Optional

- [Prebuilt binaries](https://github.com/SpAkXD/nyra/releases/latest): Linux, Windows and macOS downloads of the `nyra` tool
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpAkXD/nyra/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): build, test, and how to add a feature or an error code
